author: Hussain Nasser
headline: Venture building × AI × games in Saudi Arabia | PE & M&A modelling and valuation | Portfolio Manager, Revival Lab | Investment Director, Glo
text:
TSMC sold NT$586.9B of chips in October. A monthly record.

That's up 59.7% on October 2025 (NT$367.5B) and 14.7% on September. The previous record was August, at NT$514.8B.

January to October: NT$4,485.6B, up 43.3%.

Why I'm reading it today: Nvidia reports its quarter later today, US time. TSMC's monthly sales come out first, so I treat them as the earliest public read on chip supply. That matters for anyone buying GPUs, including the AI data centres being built in the Gulf.

Two things I'll watch:
1. Whether Nvidia's numbers show the same jump.
2. What it says about supply into 2027.

If you're planning compute in the region, which do you check first: chip supply or power?

Sources: TSMC monthly revenue reports (Oct 2025, Oct 2026); Focus Taiwan

شاركت مع الأسواق العربية - Al Arabiya Business في الحديث عن إطلاق GTA VI.

لعبة واحدة بأرقام حدث اقتصادي:
• طلبات مسبقة بنحو 15 مليون نسخة، بقيمة تقارب 1.5 مليار دولار بحسب Sensor Tower
• تقييم 99 من 100 على Metacritic
• Take-Two Interactive، المالكة لاستوديو Rockstar Games، تتوقع حجوزات بين 8 و8.2 مليار دولار هذا العام

والأثر يتجاوز الألعاب: موظفون يأخذون إجازة يوم الإطلاق، ومنصات بث تخسر جزءا من مشاهديها، ومستثمرون ينتظرون أول رقم مبيعات رسمي.

وللمنطقة حصة في القصة: مجموعة Savvy Games Group، المملوكة لصندوق الاستثمارات العامة Public Investment Fund (PIF)، تملك نحو 6% من Take-Two، والصندوق قاد أيضا الاستحواذ على Electronic Arts (EA) بقيمة 55 مليار دولار.

شكرا لقناة Al Arabiya News Channel وفريق العربية Business على الاستضافة والحوار، وشكرا لـ Hanya Amr على الدعوة.

headline: Venture building × AI × games in Saudi Arabia | PE & M&A modelling and valuation | Portfolio Manager, Revival Lab | Investment Director, Glo
text:
Acwa's Q3 net profit jumped 71%. Over nine months it's up 0.6%.

I'd read the second number first. The slides show why.

Q3 2026, from the Tadawul filing on 5 November:
Net profit: SAR 635.1M, up 71.1%
Revenue: SAR 2.2B, up 32.7%

Nine months:
Revenue: SAR 6.24B, up 16%
Net profit: SAR 1.29B, up 0.6%
Operating income: SAR 2.55B, down 8.8%

Two things stood out:

1. Timing. Acwa books development fees when projects hit milestones, and the company says milestones slipped this year. That can swing a single quarter a long way.

2. The build. Acwa has 29 projects (46.2 GW) under construction and raised SAR 30B of non-recourse funding this year. Earnings will depend on when those plants switch on, and at what funding cost.

What I'll watch: Q4 milestones and full-year operating income.

When you read a developer like this, do you start with the quarter or the year to date?

Sources: Acwa; Tadawul filing via Arab News; Enterprise
